title: Restore readable light/dark theme contrast by fixing global tokens and removing hard-coded surfaces

requirements.summary: Fix global theme tokens so surface/background colors and text colors are distinct and meet readable contrast in light and dark mode.
acceptanceCriteria: Update the CSS variables in frontend/src/index.css for both :root (light) and .dark (dark) so that background/card/popover colors are not visually similar to foreground/card-foreground/popover-foreground text colors.
Body text (text-foreground on bg-background) meets WCAG AA contrast (>= 4.5:1) in both light and dark themes.
Muted text (text-muted-foreground) remains visibly distinct from normal text and remains readable on bg-background and bg-card in both light and dark themes.
Primary/secondary/accent button combinations using *-foreground variables remain readable (no cases where button text appears close to the button background color).

file_operations.description: Update light/dark CSS variable values for background/foreground/card/popover/border/accent/muted/primary (and their *-foreground counterparts) to restore clear contrast while keeping the navy/white direction. Ensure variables are defined in a format compatible with Tailwind's theme mapping (e.g., variables used via hsl(var(--token)) should contain raw HSL channels, and variables used via oklch(var(--navy-*))) should contain raw OKLCH channels) to prevent invalid computed colors and low-contrast rendering.

requirements.summary: Remove/replace hard-coded color utility classes in key layouts so they consistently rely on theme tokens and avoid low-contrast combinations.
acceptanceCriteria: In the main app shell and authentication/landing layout (e.g., frontend/src/App.tsx), gradients/surfaces and text colors do not produce low-contrast combinations in either theme.
In shared layout components (e.g., header/footer), background and text utilities do not override the new token-based theme in a way that reduces readability (especially in dark mode).
No visible areas where headings/body text blend into their immediate container background (cards, headers, tables, panels) in both light and dark mode.

file_operations.description: Audit the authenticated shell + unauthenticated landing UI and replace hard-coded surfaces/text colors (e.g., white/gray backgrounds, dark gray overrides, text-navy overrides) with token-based utilities (bg-background/bg-card/text-foreground/text-muted-foreground/border-border, and token-aligned gradient stops) so the new global tokens fully control contrast in both themes. Keep existing overall navy/white look while avoiding any text-on-surface blending.

Replace hard-coded header surface and title colors (e.g., bg-white/gray, text-navy) with token-based background/foreground and border tokens so header readability remains consistent across light/dark mode and does not override the updated theme.

Replace hard-coded footer surface colors (e.g., bg-white/gray) and any contrast-sensitive hover overrides as needed to ensure footer text/links stay readable using the global tokens (bg-background/bg-card, text-muted-foreground, border-border) in both themes.

Update admin panel heading/title color utilities that currently hard-code navy text to instead use token-based foreground/muted-foreground utilities, ensuring headings and supporting text maintain contrast on token-based surfaces in light and dark mode.

Audit parent dashboard for hard-coded text colors (e.g., text-navy) and replace with token-based foreground/muted-foreground where appropriate. Ensure any highlighted informational surfaces (e.g., alerts) retain clear contrast with their text in both light and dark mode without relying on brittle hard-coded combinations.
